text:
Harper: Noticing a consistent clipping issue on small phones when the left rail collapses. iPhone SE / 360px: last row loses ~6px during the collapse animation. Screenshot: https://redwood-internal.screens/clip-se.png

Jae: Thanks for catching. Is the clip during animation or after?

Harper: During. The table container seems to jump when the browser chrome hides and our 100vh assumption recalculates. Also popovers sometimes render under the rail when it overlays.

Omar: Repro'd on Android Chrome emulation. Probable culprits: 100vh usage + transform-based animations that create stacking contexts. Two fixes: use visualViewport for JS-driven heights and portal popovers to body.

Lila: UX idea: introduce three behaviors instead of one breakpoint. >=520px full rail, 440-519px icon-only, <=439px overlay. This reduces sudden reflows on mid-size phones. Thoughts?

Casey: I like that. Engineering note: if we animate the rail via translateX (for perf), popovers must be portaled because transforms make new stacking contexts and clip children.

Jae: Also keep minimum touch targets >=44px. QA showed chevrons with visual size OK but tappable area below guidelines. We should expand hit area without changing visual layout.

Harper: Agreed. Small copy/a11y nits: toggle label should say "Open navigation" / "Close navigation" for screen readers. Disable hover tooltips on touch devices. And add aria-hidden on main content when overlay active.

Omar: Implementation plan: 1) portal row action popovers to root with position:fixed, 2) use env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding on lists, 3) avoid 100vh—use visualViewport.height for JS or min-height with viewport listeners, 4) CSS variables for breakpoints so Product can tweak.

Lila: Design asks: can you add sandbox variants for 360, 412, 428, 480 widths and a keyboard-only flow to validate focus trap? We also need a state where overlay auto-closes active popovers.

Casey: We'll auto-close any active row menus when the rail toggles open to avoid overlapping interactive layers. Also add an opt-in feature flag to test thresholds (440 vs 420) across devices.

Jae: Small CSS prototype I tried locally — pads the table and uses fixed-positioned sidebar when narrow. Works but popover z-index still got weird because of transform on a parent: 
```css
@media (max-width: 440px) {
  .sidebar { position: fixed; left: 0; top: var(--header-h); bottom: 0; width: 240px; transform: translateX(-100%); transition: transform .18s ease; }
  .sidebar.open { transform: translateX(0); }
  .table-container { padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom); }
}
```

Omar: That transform will create the stacking context — portaling the popover is the robust fix. When portaled, use fixed positioning and calculate anchor coords with getBoundingClientRect. Also respect prefers-reduced-motion for the rail animation.

Harper: Great. Can we aim to pick final breakpoints by EOW? If so, I'll run a quick QA pass on real devices once the sandbox variants are up.

ux-bot: Added sandbox variants (360, 412, 428, 480) and visual diff job; tags: mobile-responsive, a11y, ux.
